title: No Longer Human
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Usamaru Furuya's three-volume adaptation of Osamu Dazai's 1948 novel moves the story to present-day Tokyo. Yozo Oba, unable to show his true self, hides behind clowning and drifts from woman to woman, living off them while sinking into drink, drugs and despair. A narrator named after the artist finds Yozo's photographs and notebooks online.
life_message: None is held up directly; the story shows a life destroyed by alienation and self-hatred, asking what it means to be human.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Yozo drifts outside family and work rules entirely.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Estranged from his wealthy family; lives off strangers.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Family and social rank weigh on him but are not celebrated.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Preoccupied with authenticity and the true self.

folkways.japan: The gap between tatemae (public face) and honne (true feeling) and the shame of failing family expectations are Japanese norms the story turns into tragedy.
